extracted.intended_audience: drug and biologics sponsors; FDA (CDER/CBER) staff who manage advisory committees; prospective advisory committee members
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on organizing, staffing, operating, and documenting CDER and CBER advisory committees to implement section 505(n) of the FD&C Act (Modernization Act). Covers membership composition, conflicts of interest, meeting scheduling and quorum, action on recommendations, and training of new members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory committee membership structure (core and ad hoc)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory committee membership under the new statute is comprised of core members of the panel and other individuals who may be called upon to participate in a given meeting on an ad hoc basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core members are appointed by the Commissioner or designee based on scientific or technical expertise and serve for the duration of the committee or until their term expires, they resign, or are removed (21 CFR 14.80). Ad hoc members may be called to supplement core membership for particular meetings to provide needed expertise or representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation requirements under section 505(n)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: When supplementing core membership, the group considering an issue may include (1) representation of consumer/patient interests, (2) representation from the interests of the drug manufacturing industry, and (3) at least two members who are specialists with expertise in the particular disease or condition for which the drug under consideration is proposed to be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are to be used to ensure panels include relevant perspectives. Note: representatives of the drug manufacturing industry will not be voting members due to inherent conflict of interest concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting member qualifications and balanced composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting members have expertise as demonstrated by training, education, and experience in the subject matter the committee is considering; to the extent feasible, voting members should possess skill and experience in the development, manufacture, or use of the types of drugs to be referred to the committee, and the group should reflect a balanced composition of scientific expertise through members with diverse professional education, training, and experience (21 CFR 14.80(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core members will be voting members unless participation is prevented by conflict of interest laws and regulations. Ad hoc members who represent consumers/patients or have disease-specific expertise may vote only if they have the requisite scientific or technical expertise and no conflict-of-interest restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and selection procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Core members of advisory committees are appointed by the Commissioner or his/her designee based on their scientific or technical expertise (21 CFR 14.80). Advisory committee members who vote at committee meetings are selected in accordance with 21 CFR 14.80 and 14.82.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments may last for the duration of the committee or until term expiration, resignation, or removal. At the beginning of each meeting, voting members will be announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on voting by full-time federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: No person who is a regular full-time employee of the United States government and is engaged in the administration of the Act may be a voting member of an advisory committee (section 505(n)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory prohibition prevents federal officials administering the Act from serving as voting members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest disclosure and voting restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent a waiver, a committee member may not vote on any matter regarding the clinical investigation or approval for marketing of a drug if the member or the member's immediate family could gain financially from the committee's recommendations (section 505(n)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with conflict-of-interest rules (e.g., 18 U.S.C. 208), immediate family is defined as spouse and minor children. Members must publicly disclose all conflicts of interest with regard to issues to be considered by the committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waivers for conflicts of interest — conditions and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Waivers under section 505(n)(4) may be granted if the member's participation is necessary to afford the committee essential expertise. Such waivers may be granted by the Commissioner or designee under existing procedures that fulfill the requirements of 18 U.S.C. 208.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No waiver may be given if the member's own scientific work is involved; 'own scientific work' may include serving as principal investigator or a major participant in the clinical studies under consideration. Waiver procedures follow Chapter VIII of the Policy and Guidance Handbook for FDA Advisory Committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure of conflicts and waivers at meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: All members of an advisory committee are to disclose publicly all conflicts of interest that they may have with regard to the issues to be considered by the committee (section 505(n)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The executive secretary generally reads a statement at the beginning of each meeting stating the name of each voting member who has a conflict of interest and the type of waiver, if any, that has been granted. This practice satisfies the public disclosure requirements of section 505(n)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling/timeliness of advisory committee consideration (60-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA is to schedule advisory committee meetings so that any matter for consideration by a committee can be presented within 60 calendar days of its being ready for review (section 505(n)(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A matter is 'ready for review' when the Agency and the sponsor or applicant have completed all preparatory work for presentation. Division Directors, Chairs, and executive secretaries should anticipate and schedule meetings to comply with this statutory provision. Meetings should be planned on a yearly basis, with understanding that scheduling is tentative; advance notice is critical to ensure a quorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of electronic communications for meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: To facilitate holding advisory committee meetings, meetings may take place through the use of electronic communications such as telephone conference calls or video conferences as authorized in section 505(n)(7) and 21 CFR 14.22(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any member is unable to participate, the executive secretary may decide to go forward with the meeting as planned as long as a quorum exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quorum rules for advisory committee meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: A quorum to hold an advisory committee meeting is generally a majority of voting members. However, FDA may specify in a particular committee charter that a quorum is less than a majority of total current voting members (21 CFR 14.22(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For committees considering disparate issues, charter language can set quorum as a majority of voting members who are experts in the particular subject under consideration. When ad hoc voting members are added, quorum is based on the combined total of core members plus the added temporary voting scientific members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action on committee recommendations — 90-day notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 505(n)(8) directs the FDA official responsible for the matter to notify affected persons of the Agency's decisions on advisory committee recommendations within 90 calendar days of the committee recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary Agency decision maker (generally a Division Director or Office Director) should review the committee's recommendation and notify affected persons (sponsors of clinical investigations and/or applicants for FDA approval of drug products) of the status of FDA's decision within 90 days. If no decision has been reached, the official should notify affected persons and indicate reasons for no decision. The rationale for decisions and reasons for no decisions should be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and training requirement for new members
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 505(n)(5) directs the Agency to provide education and training to each new member of an advisory committee before the member participates in a committee meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training methods may include review of written materials and videotapes, attendance at advisory committee meetings prior to appointment, one-on-one discussions with FDA staff, orientation sessions, and CDER new reviewer training sessions. New members should be given the opportunity to attend at least one advisory committee meeting prior to appointment. Executive secretaries should convey expectations and provide appropriate orientation materials and one-on-one discussions prior to the member's first meeting participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and role clarifications (glossary items supporting procedural compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance defines key terms used for implementation (e.g., 'advisory committee', 'advisory committee member', 'affected persons', 'chair', 'core members', 'executive secretary', 'immediate family', 'panel of experts', 'primary Agency decision maker', 'ready for review').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions are to be used to interpret the procedural and substantive requirements in the guidance (for example: 'affected persons' means sponsors/applicants; 'immediate family' means spouse and minor children; 'primary Agency decision maker' identifies who must provide the 90-day notification).
